chunks: Samaʿah ibn Mihrān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About a man whom the polytheists seize, and the time of salat (prayer) comes upon him, so he fears that they will prevent him. He said: "He gestures by gesturing."

key_terms.إِيمَاءً: gesturing as a substitute for normal physical movements
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory salat (prayer) whose time has arrived
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكُونَ: the polytheists who have seized the man
key_terms.يَمْنَعُوهُ: that they stop him from performing salat (prayer)
key_terms.يُومِئُ: he performs it by making gestures

ai.seo_question: How should a captive who fears being stopped by polytheists perform salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who is unable to perform salat (prayer) normally due to fear and coercion. It shows that salat (prayer) is not dropped in such a circumstance, but is performed by indication and gesture according to one’s ability.
